Promotes public accountability and good governance in Tanzania through policy advocacy, research, capacity building, and citizen engagement. The mission is also to apply Public Social Accountability Monitoring (PSAM) analytical tool to ensure that there is proper public resources management and good governance in the country.
Expected outcomes of the program are: i)To strengthen citizen engagement in demanding Public Finance Accountability (PFA) ii)To enhance capacity of media, youth, CSOs, duty bearers and elected representatives in the practice of PFA iii)To influence policy change in improving the environment of PFA iii)To strengthen Wajibus technical and financial capacity towards making it as an effective public finance accountability think tank institution.
To achieve these outcomes mentioned above, the program will support the capacity development of civil society (users committees, local NGOs, youth, media, duty bearers and elected representatives) to implement and promote the principles of public finance accountability. Beyond, it will help establish effective collaborative links between civil society, local elected officials and technical services to ensure their participation in decision-making. As it will be better informed, civil society and the citizens will be well prepared to negotiate the inclusion during budgeting and spending of public finances.

Wajibu Institute of Public Accountability Strategic Plan 2021-2025

description.narrative:
The 2024 WAJIBU Annual Report presents a range of results, many of which align with the organizations strategic objectives, while others represent unexpected but meaningful impact. One of the core expected achievements was the increased participation of citizens in public financial accountability (PFA) processes. A total of 13,850 citizens 52% of whom were women actively participated in public dialogues across 45 villages and 15 districts. These engagements enabled communities to monitor public resource use, contribute to planning discussions, and integrate their priorities into the 2024/25 budgets through the Opportunity and Obstacles to Development (O&OD) framework.
The organization also contributed to improvements in the implementation of audit recommendations issued by the Controller and Auditor General (CAG). Nationally, the implementation rate increased from 39% to 41% in the 2022/23 financial year. A strong example comes from Dodoma City Council, where consistent engagement led to a 64% reduction in unimplemented recommendations over five years. Similarly, WAJIBUs collaboration with community radios and mainstream media contributed to widespread awareness of accountability issues, reaching over 26 million people. Notably, investigative programs on Triple A FM led to disciplinary action against civil servants in Longido District Council and revitalized a stalled hospital construction project.
Another expected result was the empowerment of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) through access to the national e-procurement system (NeST). As a result of WAJIBUs support, 38 SMEs successfully secured government tenders worth over USD 941,000, generating 408 jobs for women and youth. Furthermore, WAJIBU produced four simplified accountability reports, including Braille versions a first in Tanzania improving access to financial information for over 8,000 citizens, including people with visual impairments.
In terms of unexpected outcomes, one of the most significant was the increase in womens participation in local leadership. Following WAJIBU-led dialogues and community mobilization, 12 women were elected as village chairpersons, and several others secured positions on village councils. Stories like that of Fatuma in Kigoma and Jazila in Dodoma illustrate how social norms that had previously excluded women from public decision-making are beginning to shift. Their journeys have inspired more women to speak up and pursue leadership roles in their communities.
WAJIBUs work also led to national and global policy influence beyond original expectations. The organization successfully contributed five key recommendations to Tanzanias COP29 position paper, all of which were adopted. Additionally, WAJIBU played a central role in prompting the government to digitalize and integrate the Local Government Accountability Index into the national Integrated Monitoring and Evaluation System (IMES), reinforcing systemic transparency.
Another unexpected but important outcome was the increased responsiveness of government authorities to public concerns. When WAJIBUs reports uncovered a TZS 1.7 trillion overdraft by the government, the Minister for Finance and the Bank of Tanzania Governor issued public explanations an uncommon step that reflects growing accountability pressure. Overall, WAJIBUs 2024 results demonstrate both strategic progress and transformative shifts in civic engagement, institutional responsiveness, and inclusive governance.
